text:
### Observed differences

- Participation collapsed for three activities: A19 appeared in about 33 in 100 traces before but in only about 1 in 200 traces in the later window; A20 fell from about 29 to about 1 in 200; A25 fell from about 40 to about 1 in 200. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- Before, exactly one of A19, A20 and A25 ran in nearly every trace: pairs among the three co-occurred in only about 0.5 in 100 traces, while each of them co-occurred with A27, A28 and A29 whenever it appeared (for example A25 with A29 in 40 in 100 traces, A19 with A27 in 33 in 100). In the later window these co-occurrences dropped to about 0.5 in 100 or lower, and pairs among the three are absent from 99 in 100 traces. [REL001, REL002, REL006, REL003, REL005, REL012]
- Routing changed accordingly. Before, about 52 in 100 of A27's observed outgoing transitions went to A28 and about 44 in 100 went to one of A19, A20, A25; in the later window about 98 in 100 go straight to A28. A28's transitions to A29 rose from about 43 in 100 to 97 in 100, while its transitions to the block (about 52 in 100 before) are no longer observed. [DIR005, DIR006]
- Successions became immediate: A27 followed by A28 at distance 1 rose from about 52 in 100 to 98 in 100, A28 followed by A29 at distance 1 rose from about 43 to 96 in 100, and the A27-to-A29 distance shortened from typically 3 steps (about 90 in 100) to typically 2 steps (about 96 in 100). Before, this is consistent with the block activity sitting between A27 and A28 in about 45 in 100 traces and between A28 and A29 in about 52 in 100. [LAG001, LAG004, LAG002, DIR005, DIR006]
- A27 and A29 themselves were present in all traces in both windows and shifted only slightly in relative position (A27 mean 0.46 to 0.48; A29 mean 0.57 to 0.55). [POS004, POS005]
- A10's outgoing transition profile changed markedly: before it concentrated on A15, A47, A16, A45 and A21; in the later window it spread over roughly twenty successors, with A26 (about 17 in 100) and A45 (about 15 in 100) the largest. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the alternative block consisting of A19, A20 and A25 — from which exactly one activity was executed in nearly every earlier trace, between A27/A28 and A29 — is no longer executed in the later window, with traces proceeding directly from A27 via A28 to A29. Participation of all three activities collapsed from about 29–40 in 100 traces to about 1 in 200, A27 and A28 now lead almost exclusively to A28 and A29 respectively, and step distances collapsed to immediate succession; with 30 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected by chance, the ensemble is not what an unchanged process produces. The main limitation is that zero participation only means the activities were not observed, so a shift in case mix — an after window containing almost no traces of the variant that includes the block — cannot be ruled out; the later-window outgoing transitions of A19, A20 and A25 also rest on a single trace each and cannot be interpreted. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG004, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

Other differences: A10's outgoing behaviour changed substantially and is not part of the hypothesis above; the small relative-position shifts of A27 and A29 are consistent with the block disappearing but are minor on their own. [DIR001, POS004, POS005]
